claim: Microscopic epistasis is the tendency for the phenotype associated with a mutation to depend on the background genotype in which it emerged.
source: Laboratory evolution experiments have demonstrated the widespread prevalence of microscopic epistasis, the tendency for the phenotype associated with a mutation to depend on the background genotype in which it emerged (Khan et al., 2011; Chou et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2013; Good and Desai, 2015; Bakerlee et al., 2022; Kryazhimskiy et al., 2014; DiazColunga et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to experimental studies demonstrating microscopic epistasis.

claim: For moderate mutation rates, the overall population will consist of many competing strains because additional mutations can emerge before an existing mutation has time to fix in the culture.
source: Basic evolutionary theory indicates that for moderate mutation rates the overall population will consist of many competing strains, because additional mutations can emerge before an existing mutation has time to fix in the culture (Gerrish and Lenski, 1998; Desai and Fisher, 2007; de Visser and Rozen, 2006; Park and Krug, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to theoretical work on clonal interference.

claim: Clonal interference is consistently observed in laboratory experiments such as Lenski's long-term evolution experiment (LTEE).
source: This clonal interference is consistently observed in laboratory experiments such as Lenski's long-term evolution experiment (LTEE; Fogle et al., 2008; Lenski et al., 1991; Lenski and Travisano, 1994; Lenski, 2017; Wiser et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to experimental observations from the LTEE.

claim: The strong selection weak mutation (SSWM) limit neglects clonal interference by ensuring that the culture consists of a single dominant strain at almost all times.
source: Most theoretical studies of long-term adaptation take place in the strong selection weak mutation (SSWM) limit (Gillespie, 1983; Gillespie, 1984; Gillespie, 1991; Orr, 2002; Good et al., 2012), where the time for a beneficial mutation event to occur is large in comparison to the time for a typical beneficial mutation to fix in the population. While convenient due to analytical simplifications, this limit neglects clonal interference by ensuring that the culture consists of a single dominant strain at almost all times, and is hence known to be invalid for populations under standard laboratory conditions (de Visser and Rozen, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to theoretical work and experimental validation.

claim: The SSWM limit is known to be invalid for populations under standard laboratory conditions.
source: While convenient due to analytical simplifications, this limit neglects clonal interference by ensuring that the culture consists of a single dominant strain at almost all times, and is hence known to be invalid for populations under standard laboratory conditions (de Visser and Rozen, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to experimental work.

claim: Rugged or uncorrelated fitness landscape models posit the fitness of a mutant to be drawn at random from a fixed distribution.
source: To avoid the analytical and computational challenges associated with modeling the genome at microscopic granularity, significant theoretical effort has been spent studying macroscopic "rugged" or uncorrelated models (Kauffman and Levin, 1987; Kauffman and Weinberger, 1989; Wilke, 2004; Macken and Perelson, 1989; Flyvbjerg and Lautrup, 1992; Kingman, 1978), which posit the fitness of a mutant to be drawn at random from a fixed distribution (Park and Krug, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to theoretical work on rugged fitness landscapes.

claim: Fitness-parameterized models assume the distribution of fitness effects (DFE) depends only on the fitness of the parent.
source: More recently, macroscopic "fitness-parameterized" models, which assume the distribution of fitness effects (DFE) depends only on the fitness of the parent, have garnered interest as a way to model correlations in the fitness landscape (Kryazhimskiy et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to theoretical work on fitness-parameterized models.

claim: Rugged landscapes make predictions that violate experimental measurements, such as the typical length of an adaptive walk.
source: Rugged landscapes make predictions that are known to violate experimental measurements, such as the typical length of an adaptive walk (Orr, 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to work comparing theoretical predictions with experimental observations.

claim: Microscopic models treat the genome as a sequence of loci each with a binary label indicating the presence or absence of a mutation.
source: One approach that corrects the deficiencies of macroscopic models is the use of microscopic models, which treat the genome as a sequence of loci each with a binary label indicating the presence or absence of a mutation.
evidence: The claim is a direct statement about the definition of microscopic models.

claim: The NK model is the most well-studied microscopic model in evolutionary theory.
source: Perhaps the most well-studied microscopic model in evolutionary theory is Kauffmans NK model (Kauffman and Levin, 1987), but similar microscopic models can be obtained systematically via Fourier expansion (Neher and Shraiman, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to the NK model and related work.

claim: Microscopic models can be obtained systematically via Fourier expansion.
source: Perhaps the most well-studied microscopic model in evolutionary theory is Kauffmans NK model (Kauffman and Levin, 1987), but similar microscopic models can be obtained systematically via Fourier expansion (Neher and Shraiman, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to work on Fourier expansion approaches.

claim: Spin glass models have been used to study the role of epistasis in adaptive dynamics, leading to insight into the generation of slow, logarithmic fitness trajectories.
source: Recently, spin glass models have been used to study the role of epistasis in adaptive dynamics, leading to insight into the generation of slow, logarithmic fitness trajectories (Guo et al., 2019) and into how macroscopic epistasis emerges from widespread microscopic interactions (Reddy and Desai, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to recent work using spin glass models.

claim: Prior spin glass studies of adaptive dynamics make the SSWM assumption due to the computational expense of full-scale microscopic simulations.
source: But due to the computational expense of full-scale microscopic simulations, these prior works make the SSWM assumption, which greatly simplifies the resulting adaptive dynamics to a process that is analytically tractable.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the stated limitations of prior work.

claim: The study presents a systematic numerical study of the evolutionary dynamics of a microbial culture under serial dilution on a microscopic fitness landscape far from the SSWM regime.
source: In order to understand the role played by microscopic epistasis and clonal interference in real-world evolving populations, we present a systematic numerical study of the evolutionary dynamics of a microbial culture under serial dilution on a microscopic fitness landscape far from the SSWM regime.
evidence: The claim describes the main contribution of the study.

claim: The model contains both additive and epistatic terms, and the relative magnitude of the two terms can be adjusted.
source: To do so, we consider a spin glass type model that enables us to independently tune the magnitude of epistasis and the level of clonal interference in the culture. The model contains both additive and epistatic terms. The relative magnitude of the two terms can be adjusted, and the epistatic interaction takes place pairwise between two loci on the genome.
evidence: The claim describes a feature of the model used in the study.

claim: The epistatic interaction takes place pairwise between two loci on the genome.
source: The model contains both additive and epistatic terms. The relative magnitude of the two terms can be adjusted, and the epistatic interaction takes place pairwise between two loci on the genome.
evidence: The claim describes a feature of the model used in the study.

claim: The study developed a high-performance, OpenMP-based multi-threaded implementation of the stochastic process in C++.
source: To resolve the adaptive dynamics, we develop a high-performance, OpenMP-based multi-threaded implementation of the resulting stochastic process in C++ (https://github.com/nmboffi/spin_glass_evodyn copy archived at Boffi, 2023), which we use to study an adaptive walk to a fitness peak comprising a few hundred fixation events.
evidence: The claim describes a methodological contribution of the study.

claim: The implementation leverages an efficient algorithm for computation of the fitness that leverages the structure of the epistatic interaction.
source: The implementation leverages several algorithmic advances to capture the complete microscopic details of the process over long timescales: an efficient algorithm for computation of the fitness that leverages the structure of the epistatic interaction, a hashing-based method for storage of strains by genotype for fast splitting and joining, and an efficient approach for diluting the culture.
evidence: The claim describes a technical feature of the implementation.

claim: The implementation uses a hashing-based method for storage of strains by genotype for fast splitting and joining.
source: The implementation leverages several algorithmic advances to capture the complete microscopic details of the process over long timescales: an efficient algorithm for computation of the fitness that leverages the structure of the epistatic interaction, a hashing-based method for storage of strains by genotype for fast splitting and joining, and an efficient approach for diluting the culture.
evidence: The claim describes a technical feature of the implementation.

claim: The algorithmic advances render tractable the computation of the entire distribution of fitness effects, the complete sequence of fixed mutations along with their individual effects, and the number of remaining beneficial mutations for any strain at any time with realistic population sizes (one hundred million bacteria) over realistic timescales (tens of thousands of generations).
source: These algorithmic advances render tractable the computation of the entire distribution of fitness effects, the complete sequence of fixed mutations along with their individual effects, and the number of remaining beneficial mutations for any strain at any time with realistic population sizes (one hundred million bacteria) over realistic timescales (tens of thousands of generations).
evidence: The claim describes the capabilities enabled by the implementation.

claim: Hill-climbing dynamics on a random and sparse fitness landscape with two-point interactions cannot give rise to the slow, low-exponent power law trajectories observed in Lenski's LTEE even with clonal interference.
source: To this end, we show that hill-climbing dynamics on a random and sparse fitness landscape with two-point interactions cannot give rise to the slow, low-exponent power law trajectories observed in Lenskis LTEE even with clonal interference, suggesting that other factors such as structured interactions might be at play.
evidence: The claim is a finding from the study's simulations and analysis.

claim: Any macroscopic fitness-parameterized model used to describe a microscopic process must depend intrinsically on the level of clonal interference in the population.
source: Moreover, we show that any macroscopic fitness-parameterized model used to describe a microscopic process must depend intrinsically on the level of clonal interference in the population, implying that the DFE in a macroscopic model for an experimental system must be tuned to the mutation rate of the culture.
evidence: The claim is a finding from the study's analysis.

claim: The DFE in a macroscopic model for an experimental system must be tuned to the mutation rate of the culture.
source: Moreover, we show that any macroscopic fitness-parameterized model used to describe a microscopic process must depend intrinsically on the level of clonal interference in the population, implying that the DFE in a macroscopic model for an experimental system must be tuned to the mutation rate of the culture.
evidence: The claim is an implication derived from the study's findings.

claim: Stronger microscopic epistasis gives rise to fitness trajectories with slower growth independent of the number of competing strains.
source: Through extensive numerical experimentation, we find that stronger microscopic epistasis gives rise to fitness trajectories with slower growth independent of the number of competing strains, which we quantify with power-law fits and understand mechanistically via a random walk model that neglects dynamical correlations between genes.
evidence: The claim is a main finding from the study's numerical experiments.

claim: Increasing the level of clonal interference leads to fitness trajectories with faster growth (in functional form) without microscopic epistasis.
source: We show that increasing the level of clonal interference leads to fitness trajectories with faster growth (in functional form) without microscopic epistasis, but leaves the rate of growth invariant when epistasis is sufficiently strong, indicating that the role of clonal interference depends intimately on the underlying fitness landscape.
evidence: The claim is a main finding from the study.

claim: Increasing the level of clonal interference leaves the rate of growth invariant when epistasis is sufficiently strong.
source: We show that increasing the level of clonal interference leads to fitness trajectories with faster growth (in functional form) without microscopic epistasis, but leaves the rate of growth invariant when epistasis is sufficiently strong, indicating that the role of clonal interference depends intimately on the underlying fitness landscape.
evidence: The claim is a main finding from the study.

claim: The role of clonal interference depends intimately on the underlying fitness landscape.
source: We show that increasing the level of clonal interference leads to fitness trajectories with faster growth (in functional form) without microscopic epistasis, but leaves the rate of growth invariant when epistasis is sufficiently strong, indicating that the role of clonal interference depends intimately on the underlying fitness landscape.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the study's findings.

claim: Realistic biological fitness landscapes are thought to be rugged, containing many local extrema.
source: Realistic biological fitness landscapes are thought to be rugged, containing many local extrema.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge in evolutionary biology.

claim: The study uses a batch culture subject to a standard serial dilution protocol.
source: We study a batch culture subject to a standard serial dilution protocol (Lenski et al., 1991; Lin et al., 2020; Desai et al., 2007; Kryazhimskiy et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim describes the experimental protocol modeled in the study, supported by citations.

claim: The study fixes the initial rank to 100 because typically only a fraction of possible mutations are beneficial.
source: Because typically only a fraction of possible mutations are beneficial, we fix the initial rank to 100.
evidence: The claim describes a parameter choice in the study based on biological reasoning.

claim: Equation 1 represents the two lowest-order terms in a Fourier expansion of an arbitrary function defined on the Boolean hypercube.
source: Equation 1 represents the two lowest-order terms in a Fourier expansion of an arbitrary function defined on the Boolean hypercube (Neher and Shraiman, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to work on Fourier expansions.

claim: The model represents a rigorously quantifiable approximation of any choice of fitness model defined on the hypercube.
source: As such, our model represents a rigorously quantifiable approximation of any choice of fitness model defined on the hypercube.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the Fourier expansion property.

claim: For low mutation rate, the population is in the SSWM regime and the evolutionary dynamics correspond to sequential sweeps of beneficial mutations throughout the population, which consists of a single dominant strain.
source: For low mutation rate, the population is in the SSWM regime and the evolutionary dynamics correspond to sequential sweeps of beneficial mutations throughout the population, which consists of a single dominant strain (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim describes a property of the model at low mutation rates, supported by Figure 1D.

claim: As the mutation rate increases, the adaptation dynamics become richer, enabling higher-order effects such as multiple mutations, stochastic tunneling, and competing populations.
source: As the mutation rate increases, the adaptation dynamics become richer, enabling higher-order effects such as multiple mutations (Weissman et al., 2009), stochastic tunneling (Iwasa et al., 2004; Guo et al., 2019), and competing populations, all of which emerge naturally in our simulations.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations and describes observations from the simulations.

claim: The fitness of a given strain may be computed as a correction to the fitness of a reference strain that is updated adaptively to track the state of the population.
source: Leveraging algebraic simplifications intrinsic to the model's mathematical structure, the fitness of a given strain may be computed as a correction to the fitness of a reference strain that is updated adaptively to track the state of the population.
evidence: The claim describes a computational technique used in the study.

claim: The adaptive fast fitness computation is several orders of magnitude faster than a naive calculation.
source: The resulting adaptive fast fitness computation is several orders of magnitude faster than a naive calculation, and our ability to simulate to long times in the strong clonal interference regime hinges upon it.
evidence: The claim describes the performance advantage of the computational technique.

claim: The fitness trajectory takes more time to approach its asymptotic value as β increases, indicating a slower approach towards equilibrium.
source: The fitness trajectory takes more time to approach its asymptotic value as β increases, indicating a slower approach towards equilibrium (Figure 2A/B).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations from Figure 2A/B.

claim: Higher values of β lead to a greater number of fixed mutations.
source: The substitution trajectories demonstrate that increasing the amount of microscopic epistasis smoothly leads to an accumulation of more fixed mutations at each time.
evidence: The claim is supported by observations from the substitution trajectories.

claim: As β increases, a greater number of new available beneficial mutations are generated per each typical fixation event.
source: Because the initial rank (the number of available beneficial mutations) is identical for each value of β, the substitution trajectories suggest a simple picture: as β increases, a greater number of new available beneficial mutations are generated per each typical fixation event.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the substitution trajectory data.

claim: Because more mutations are needed to cease adaptation, each typical fixation event must provide less progress towards the fitness peak as β increases.
source: Moreover, because more mutations are needed to cease adaptation, each typical fixation event must provide less progress towards the fitness peak.
evidence: The claim is a logical inference from the observation about the number of mutations.

claim: Flat regions in the fitness landscape have been identified as a source of slow dynamics in previous studies of spin-glass physics.
source: Mathematically, this corresponds to a greater prevalence of flat regions in the fitness landscape, which have been identified as a source of slow dynamics in previous studies of spin-glass physics (Kurchan and Laloux, 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to spin-glass physics literature.

claim: The reduction to a few-parameter fitness-parameterized model has been justified both theoretically and experimentally in the clonal interference regime.
source: The reduction to a few-parameter fitness-parameterized model has been justified both theoretically (Good et al., 2012) and experimentally (Hegreness et al., 2006) in the clonal interference regime, and we find that it similarly provides useful insight in the SSWM regime.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to theoretical and experimental work.

claim: For all nonzero values of β, the expected beneficial increment behaves linearly as a function of fitness in both mutation regimes.
source: In both mutation regimes, for all nonzero values of β, the expected beneficial increment behaves linearly as a function of fitness (Figure 3B/D).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations from Figure 3B/D.

claim: The linear behavior of the expected beneficial increment as a function of fitness is known as macroscopic or global epistasis.
source: This phenomenon is known as macroscopic or global epistasis, and has been shown to be an emergent property of a class of finite-sites models similar to the one considered here (Reddy and Desai, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to work on global epistasis.

claim: At any fixed relative distance from the fitness peak, beneficial mutation events become more rare as β increases.
source: This indicates that at any fixed relative distance from the fitness peak, beneficial mutation events become more rare as β increases.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the rank data.

claim: Microscopic epistasis leads to a slower fitness trajectory through two complementary effects: at each fixed value of fitness, beneficial mutations are less likely to be found by random mutation, and more of them are required to reach the peak due to a lower typical (normalized) increment.
source: Taken together, these observations demonstrate that microscopic epistasis leads to a slower fitness trajectory through two complementary effects. At each fixed value of fitness, beneficial mutations are less likely to be found by random mutation; moreover, more of them are required to reach the peak due to a lower typical (normalized) increment.
evidence: The claim is a synthesis of the observations about rank and expected increment.

claim: Additional beneficial mutations are generated by the epistatic interaction as each fixation event occurs.
source: These additional beneficial mutations are generated by the epistatic interaction as each fixation event occurs.
evidence: The claim is an inference about the mechanism of mutation generation.

claim: The mechanism by which microscopic epistasis slows the trajectory is common to both the SSWM and clonal interference regimes.
source: The previous sections highlighted that the mechanism is common to both the SSWM and clonal interference regimes, for which reason we restrict to the SSWM limit in the subsequent analysis.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the previous results.

claim: In the absence of microscopic epistasis, each fixation event would decrease the rank by one until all available beneficial mutations have fixed.
source: In the absence of microscopic epistasis, each such fixation event would decrease the rank by one until all available beneficial mutations have fixed.
evidence: The claim is a logical consequence of the model without epistasis.

claim: Previous studies in spin glass and electron glass physics have obtained significant physical insight by neglecting dynamical correlations.
source: Previous studies in spin glass (Horner, 2007; Eastham et al., 2006) and electron glass (Mogilyanskii and Raikh, 1989; Amir et al., 2008) physics have obtained significant physical insight by neglecting these dynamical correlations, and here we take a similar approach.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to physics literature.

claim: The random walk model predicts a monotonically decreasing exponent and a monotonically increasing number of fixed mutations as a function of β.
source: Fitting the power law in Equation 2 to the mean fitness trajectories shows that the random walk model predicts a monotonically decreasing exponent and a monotonically increasing number of fixed mutations as a function of β (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by results shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The random walk model is qualitatively consistent with the results of applying the same coarse-grained simulation approach in the SSWM approximation to the full fitness model.
source: This is qualitatively consistent with the results of applying the same coarse-grained simulation approach in the SSWM approximation to the full fitness model (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison with Figure 4B.

claim: Due to the neglect of correlations, the random walk model predicts a lower number of generated beneficial mutations and a correspondingly higher fitness exponent.
source: Due to the neglect of correlations, the random walk model predicts a lower number of generated beneficial mutations and a correspondingly higher fitness exponent.
evidence: The claim is a comparison between the random walk model and the full model.

claim: The transport in Equation 5 is asymmetric because only beneficial mutations can fix in the SSWM limit.
source: Because only beneficial mutations can fix in the SSWM limit, the transport in Equation 5 is asymmetric, and beneficial mutations will be rapidly converted to deleterious mutations with equal magnitude but opposite sign.
evidence: The claim is a logical consequence of the SSWM assumption.

claim: The noise in Equation 7 broadens the distribution of fitness increments, which converts deleterious mutations with small magnitude into beneficial mutations with small magnitude and vice-versa.
source: The noise in Equation 7 broadens the distribution of fitness increments, which converts deleterious mutations with small magnitude into beneficial mutations with small magnitude and vice-versa.
evidence: The claim describes a mechanism in the random walk model.

claim: The buildup of deleterious mutations results in a diffusive flux from the deleterious half to the beneficial half, providing a simple mechanism for the formation of new beneficial mutations.
source: The buildup of deleterious mutations results in a diffusive flux from the deleterious half to the beneficial half, providing a simple mechanism for the formation of new beneficial mutations (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim describes a mechanism illustrated in Figure 4C.

claim: Clonal interference is known to reduce fixation probabilities.
source: Clonal interference is known to reduce fixation probabilities (Gerrish and Lenski, 1998; Lin et al., 2020), and hence to slow down the rate of adaptation when compared to an SSWM model with the same parameters.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to work on clonal interference.

claim: Clonal interference slows down the rate of adaptation when compared to an SSWM model with the same parameters.
source: Clonal interference is known to reduce fixation probabilities (Gerrish and Lenski, 1998; Lin et al., 2020), and hence to slow down the rate of adaptation when compared to an SSWM model with the same parameters.
evidence: The claim is a logical consequence of reduced fixation probabilities.

claim: Models incorporating both clonal interference and macroscopic epistasis have been developed to predict the slow power law fitness trajectory observed in Lenski's long-term evolution experiment.
source: Given its prevalence in realistic evolving laboratory populations, models incorporating both clonal interference and macroscopic epistasis have been developed to predict the slow power law fitness trajectory observed in Lenski's long-term evolution experiment (Wiser et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to modeling work.

claim: The effect of clonal interference on the shape of the fitness trajectory is still poorly understood.
source: Despite this interest, the effect of clonal interference on the shape of the fitness trajectory is still poorly understood.
evidence: The claim is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: In fitness-parameterized models, for sufficiently weak clonal interference, the way clonal interference affects the shape of the fitness trajectory depends on how the beneficial mutation rate changes with fitness.
source: In fitness-parameterized models, for sufficiently weak clonal interference, the way clonal interference affects the shape of the fitness trajectory depends on how the beneficial mutation rate changes with fitness (Guo and Amir, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to theoretical work.

claim: For typical fitness-parameterized models where beneficial mutations become less prevalent as the population climbs up the hill, clonal interference accelerates the fitness trajectory.
source: In particular, for typical models where beneficial mutations become less prevalent as the population climbs up the hill, clonal interference accelerates the fitness trajectory.
evidence: The claim is a statement about predictions from fitness-parameterized models.

claim: The effect of clonal interference on the fitness trajectory depends on the strength of microscopic epistasis.
source: Here, we demonstrate that the effect of clonal interference on the fitness trajectory depends on the strength of microscopic epistasis.
evidence: The claim is a main finding of the study.

claim: In the absence of microscopic epistasis, clonal interference is seen to accelerate the trajectory.
source: In its absence, clonal interference is seen to accelerate the trajectory, while for a sufficiently strong epistatic interaction, clonal interference does not quantitatively affect the speed of the trajectory.
evidence: The claim is a finding from the study.

claim: For a sufficiently strong epistatic interaction, clonal interference does not quantitatively affect the speed of the trajectory.
source: In its absence, clonal interference is seen to accelerate the trajectory, while for a sufficiently strong epistatic interaction, clonal interference does not quantitatively affect the speed of the trajectory.
evidence: The claim is a finding from the study.

claim: Increasing the mutation rate increases clonal interference, but also accelerates adaptation by allowing for more mutations each day.
source: Increasing the mutation rate increases clonal interference, but also accelerates adaptation by allowing for more mutations each day.
evidence: The claim describes a property of the model.

claim: Normalizing time by the mutation rate eliminates the effect of more mutations per day and isolates the role of clonal interference itself.
source: This effect can be eliminated by normalizing time by the mutation rate, so as to isolate the role of clonal interference itself.
evidence: The claim describes a methodological approach.

claim: Viewed in units normalized by mutation rate, clonal interference decelerates the fitness trajectory due to the suppression of fixation probabilities.
source: Viewed in these units, clonal interference decelerates the fitness trajectory due to the suppression of fixation probabilities (Appendix 1—figure 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by Appendix 1—figure 1.

claim: The effective macroscopic model depends on the mutation rate, which is typically treated as an independent parameter in the standard fitness-parameterized framework.
source: This mapping reveals a striking observation: the effective macroscopic model depends on the mutation rate, which is typically treated as an independent parameter in the standard fitness-parameterized framework.
evidence: The claim is a finding from the mapping to fitness-parameterized landscapes.

claim: In both the epistatic and non-epistatic landscapes, the distribution becomes more sharply peaked for higher levels of clonal interference, while it has a heavier tail for lower levels.
source: In both the epistatic and non-epistatic landscapes, we find that the distribution becomes more sharply peaked for higher levels of clonal interference, while it has a heavier tail for lower levels (Figure 6A/B).
evidence: The claim is supported by observations from Figure 6A/B.

claim: Clonal interference suppresses the fixation of low-effect mutations.
source: This occurs because clonal interference suppresses the fixation of low-effect mutations.
evidence: The claim is an explanation for the observed distribution changes.

claim: In both landscapes, the expected increment tends to decrease with increasing μ at fixed fitness.
source: Both with and without epistasis, the expected increment tends to decrease with increasing µ at fixed fitness, capturing the fact that higher µ favors the fixation of mutations with higher effect.
evidence: The claim is supported by observations from Figure 6C/D.

claim: Higher μ favors the fixation of mutations with higher effect.
source: Both with and without epistasis, the expected increment tends to decrease with increasing µ at fixed fitness, capturing the fact that higher µ favors the fixation of mutations with higher effect.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the expected increment behavior.

claim: Without epistasis, the rank increases with μ at fixed fitness.
source: Without epistasis, the rank increases with increasing µ at fixed fitness.
evidence: The claim is supported by observations from Figure 6E.

claim: With epistasis, the rank curves behave non-monotonically in μ at fixed fitness, and become comparable at high fitness.
source: With epistasis, the rank curves behave non-monotonically in µ at fixed fitness, and become comparable at high fitness.
evidence: The claim is supported by observations from Figure 6F.

claim: The simulation approach gives the ability to probe microscopic details that are challenging to obtain experimentally, such as statistics of the distribution of fitness effects and the rank over time.
source: Our simulation approach gives us the ability to probe microscopic details that are challenging to obtain experimentally, such as statistics of the distribution of fitness effects and the rank over time.
evidence: The claim describes an advantage of the simulation approach.

claim: The approach allows study of regimes such as strong microscopic epistasis and strong clonal interference that have eluded previous theoretical study.
source: The approach also allows us to study regimes such as strong microscopic epistasis and strong clonal interference that have eluded previous theoretical study.
evidence: The claim describes an advantage of the simulation approach.

claim: As the strength of microscopic epistasis increases, the beneficial mutation rate becomes an increasingly linear function of fitness, similar to the phenomenon of global epistasis observed for the expected beneficial fitness increment.
source: A by-product of our analysis is an observation that, as microscopic epistasis increases in strength, the beneficial mutation rate becomes an increasingly linear function of fitness, similar to the phenomenon of global epistasis observed for the expected beneficial fitness increment (Reddy and Desai, 2021).
evidence: The claim is a finding from the study, supported by a citation.

claim: The strength of epistasis in realistic microbial populations could be inferred by measuring the beneficial mutation rate as a function of fitness experimentally.
source: This suggests that the strength of epistasis in realistic microbial populations could be inferred by measuring the beneficial mutation rate as a function of fitness experimentally.
evidence: The claim is a suggestion based on the study's findings.

claim: The behavior of the beneficial mutation rate as a function of fitness plays a central role in setting the speed of the fitness trajectory.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that the behavior of the beneficial mutation rate as a function of fitness plays a central role in setting the speed of the fitness trajectory.
evidence: The claim is a synthesis of the study's findings.

claim: This relation provides a novel link between standard techniques in spin glass physics and microscopic population genetics.
source: This relation provides a novel link between standard techniques in spin glass physics and microscopic population genetics.
evidence: The claim is an interpretation of the mathematical relation.

claim: In spin glasses, the two-point correlation function often exhibits stretched exponential relaxations.
source: This stands in contrast to the standard setting in spin glasses, where the two-point correlation function often exhibits stretched exponential relaxations (Phillips, 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to spin glass literature.

claim: It is sufficient to consider the two-point correlation function, or equivalently the substitution trajectory, and no additional information is contained in the four-point correlator.
source: This demonstrates that it is sufficient to consider the two-point correlation function, or equivalently the substitution trajectory, and that no additional information is contained in the four-point correlator.
evidence: The claim is an inference from the relationship between χ_2 and χ_4.

claim: Horizontal gene transfer may have a similar effect to microscopic epistasis by allowing large jumps across the fitness landscape, and could slow the fitness trajectory by generating groups of new beneficial mutations.
source: One possibility is to allow for horizontal gene transfer between bacterial strains. By allowing large jumps across the fitness landscape, horizontal gene transfer may have a similar effect to microscopic epistasis, and could slow the fitness trajectory by generating groups of new beneficial mutations (Slomka et al., 2020); on the other hand, it could also accelerate the fitness trajectory by allowing for larger steps towards a fitness maximum.
evidence: The claim is a speculation about future work, supported by a citation.

claim: Horizontal gene transfer could also accelerate the fitness trajectory by allowing for larger steps towards a fitness maximum.
source: By allowing large jumps across the fitness landscape, horizontal gene transfer may have a similar effect to microscopic epistasis, and could slow the fitness trajectory by generating groups of new beneficial mutations (Slomka et al., 2020); on the other hand, it could also accelerate the fitness trajectory by allowing for larger steps towards a fitness maximum.
evidence: The claim is a speculation about future work.

claim: It would be interesting to carefully probe the value of β for which the effect of clonal interference vanishes, and to determine if this occurs as a sharp phase transition or if there is a gradual decay of the effect of clonal interference with β.
source: It would be interesting to carefully probe the value of β for which the effect of clonal interference vanishes, and to determine if this occurs as a sharp phase transition or if there is a gradual decay of the effect of clonal interference with β.
evidence: The claim is a suggestion for future work.

claim: Understanding the behavior of how the effect of clonal interference depends on β could lead to a way to measure the strength of epistasis in experimental systems, by studying how the fitness trajectory depends on the level of clonal interference.
source: Understanding this behavior could lead to a way to measure the strength of epistasis in experimental systems, by studying how the fitness trajectory depends on the level of clonal interference.
evidence: The claim is a speculation about potential applications.
